item.content:encoded:

Interesting SCP you've got there!

Critiqued it…

+ show block

I hate it.

Just kidding! I love this concept! It's super intriguing, and definitely something I want to read! The only problem is it's been done before with SCP-694. Although, I think your idea could be salvaged if you came up with a more specific storyline. Maybe you could have a foundation agent or D-Class trapped in the time loop? Trying to reach out and record each day? But slowly starts fading away into the redundancy? Maybe he dies every single time loop? Maybe they're something, like an entity in the middle of it all, controlling everything?

This concept is fabulous, but you need to make it a bit more unique before I go ahead and greenlight it. Please take your time to think up what you believe to be an interesting plotline, and go ahead and pm me once you've editted your original post and if you want me to take another look!
Best of luck!

item.title: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction: Re: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction
item.content:encoded:
Hi caspian2,

It is my fault for not explaining thoroughly enough. The reason I decided to use thumbnails that can change depending on what the viewer finds intriguing is because I want to relate this to a concept that is seen on real video-sharing websites which is clickbait, where the thumbnails are often misleading or anticlimactic.

Your advice is again extremely helpful and I think I can incorporate it into my SCP. For example, with the idea of a dead loved one from his/her past, if the viewer deeply misses a dead loved one, than the SCP could create a thumbnail that seemingly provides closure for the viewer. Of course, it is a trap and the viewer becomes another victim.

For your other question of why is it doing this, I have come up with an idea that again relates to the concept of clickbait. Most people who use clickbait thumbnails usually are trying to make money. So, to incorporate this into the SCP, the SCP is kidnapping people using its anomalous effects and is selling them on the black market. At some point, the SCP Foundation intervenes and manages to rescue a victim. The SCP Foundation realizes that there has to be a mastermind behind this SCP, however the victim they save is severely injured and has been administered with amnestics.

Once again, I greatly appreciate all the advice and help you have given me so far. Please offer more advice that you think I may need.

item.title: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

-Anomalous statue with "Are We Cool Yet" carved into the bottom. Occasionally 'activates', creating a memetic aura causing a variety of effects in people around them. Note attached, filled with nonsensical writing "explaining" the artistic significance of the statue. The effects are assumed by the Foundation to be some kind of pretentious commentary, as most AWCY projects are, and try to figure out what it all means in an attempt to stop its effects or discover its creator.

-Is eventually revealed to be an in-universe parody of AWCY, likely made by a member of ACWY as a sort of self-own after it stops its effects and is reclassified as neutralised.

Central Narrative:

-Foundation attempts to interpret the effects of the statue, researching increasingly obscure art pieces and reaching more and more in an attempt to work out what the artist was trying to say.

-One of the statues effects makes the researchers think the statue is prophesying some catastrophic event, fuelled by their own (justified, at this point) paranoia, and begin kidnapping and interrogating AWCY members to no avail.

+ show block
– hide block

-Their interpretations become ridiculously complex in a search for some kind of cohesive meaning, matching the actual effects of the statue becoming more nonsensical and racking up a larger body count in the process. Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason, before stopping completely.

-Item is reclassified as "Safe" or "neutralized" and the foundation eventually works out that they have inadvertently been led on a wild goose chase, and deduce the item was meant as a parody of AWCY themselves- meaningless effects resulting in unnecessarily deaths and a note pretentiously explaining the work.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

-The items effects are extremely weird and nonsensical, and the foundation's interpretations of the items effects cross-link other SCP's and reference various societal or historical events, phenomenon, and art pieces.

-As far as I could tell there aren't any AWCY scips that directly make fun of their own group, which seems something right up their alley.

Additional Notes:

-Started as a GAW project, but I prefer it as an actual AWCY member making fun of the group he's apart of.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight): Re: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM request: Sorry if I'm late!
That's an interesting SCP you got there
Would be a shame if someone
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

I hate to be a sore thumb, but unless you make a some major changes, I don't see this as being a successful idea. Your base concept is okay, but its severely lacking in characters, themes, and the general appeal that stories have. What you have right now, at least to me, seems like a glorified mash of a museum and haunted house, which aren't the most original combination. Granted, I'm not exactly into history, which may be why I find the idea so lackluster.

What is SCP trying to prove? That colonialism/slavery/war/etc were terrible and tragic? Most people know that. I feel like you need to take this a step beyond what you currently have. Beyond simple ghosts and demons and classic, cheap horror. You need something real for your audience.

Here's an alternate idea that you can choose to reject/accept:
Each floor of the room causes the participant to physically enter a pocket dimension, where they reenact a scene from the particular era of the floor. For instance, for the 1500s to 1600s, have the person that enters the hall be chased by bloodhounds and and a white man. Maybe have their family running with them, and maybe their son falls behind. The person turns back and attempts to find the son, but sees the dogs have already torn into him. The person turns back and starts running again, and they can hear bullets hitting tree trunks beside their heads, and the thunder of hoofbeats behind them. They try to keep running forward, barefoot and near naked, but they feel a pain in their back, and see blood seeping out of their chest, where they'd been hit by a bullet. The person then falls over, and feels a boot on his head. In front of him, he can see his family still being chased, and he knows they won't make it. He feels a rifle on his head, and with a bang, everything goes black.

When the person wakes up again, they'll find themselves in an empty room with a door. They'll open the door and descend down a flight of stairs, after which they relive another terrifying and tragic scenario. And for added elements of horror, have it so that there's no way to leave. The person can only go forward. They'll be trapped in there, experiencing history forever and ever. And there's not much they can do about it.

Of course you don't need to take that idea, but you need to evoke some sort of emotional response in your audience, especially if you want to make an emotional impact, which is something I feel you want to do.

I'm not going to give this idea a greenlight, at least not yet. But if you go back and refine it, an give some more details, I'll come back and give it a second look. Please PM me with any questions/comments/concerns, and best of luck!

item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM request
Interesting SCP you got here!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

Not gonna lie, I'm digging this idea! A Foundation clone. Or the original foundation that the Foundation was cloned from. who knows? This article is going to be like a dog chasing its tail. Or a tail chasing a dog. It's sure to be a fascinating, mildly infuriating, but nonetheless fun article to see!
You seem to have a solid narrative. Wouldn't it be funny if at the same time SCP was infiltrating the PCS, the PCS was infiltrating the SCP? I kind of like Cybersqyd's idea of having the PCS be an extension of the SCP Foundation and the MTF just raids their own base. Since the two organizations are backronyms of each other, I doubt that such an occurrence could be chalked up to chance. Maybe have some sort of implications or hypotheses to throughout the story? Like the PCS is from an alternate dimension, or both groups are old rivals, or that they're the same organization. Something like that to bring the reader full circle.
I think you have a solid narrative and all. I'm going to just go ahead and give you a tentative greenlight, although I would like you to be a bit more concise with the details. Please feel free to reach out with any questions, and do keep me posted!

item.title: SCP Idea - Security Blanket: Re: SCP Idea - Security Blanket
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM
Hey Blackwater!
Interesting SCP you've got here!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

I can certainly see this as a successful SCP, and the concept/narrative of the blanket being the only thing the boy has connecting him to his family is quite intriguing, and potentially emotional. That being said, there are a few places that your story could be tweaked a bit. A lot of them are similar to Red's, and I'd advising re-reading his post to make sure you improve your concept as much as possible.

  • Omnipotence:The blanket does seem to have too much power. For one thing, I'm thinking having the blanket be able to make the boy invisible, invincible, and capable of returning to him a bit much. I'd say scrap one or all of these traits, since they don't seem to be adding much to the story.
  • Mystery: Why are the creatures chasing the blanket? I get the hole mystery of the unknown thing, but I think your story would be a bit more impactful if you gave a reason for why that was happening, and possibly tied it into the backstory of the boy's family
  • Narrative: The anomalous properties of the SCP are important to your article, but the story contained in it is the most important part. Make sure you focus on the emotions, characters, and themes behind your story.
  • Greenlights: From what I can see, you're a first time author. If that's true, I'd say "yes" for seeking greenlights, since you need two to get your concept afloat. I'd definitely be willing to do so if you fixed a couple of things up!

Please keep in mind that this critique isn't meant to bash on you or your writing. It's a great core concept, as far as I'm concerned, and I can definitely see it becoming a popular SCP. It just needs a few tweaks and you're good to go! Please do reach out to me and any other butterfly squad members. After all, we're here to help!

item.title: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction: Re: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction
item.content:encoded:
Hi Costansin,

I've read your revised concept on the forums. It's definitely more detailed in terms of the discovery and test logs on the laptop. You've described how the scp works in alot of detail, but we still don't understand why it's doing this and why is it choosing its victims at random. Okay, so they watch a video that's "intriguing" to them? So what? It's goal is simply to get as many victims as possible?

Consider revising the way the laptop picks / chooses its victims, especially since you're going for a mind-affecting anomaly. For example, could it be that the laptop allows a user to chat with a dead loved one from his/her past? This is a more natural way of engaging a user without having to affect his/her mind. An alternative would be for the previous user (now a prisoner in the laptop) to communicate with the new victim in order to trick him/her to take their place. You see where I'm going with this? Your anomalous effects should be connected in some way. Instead, they still seem entirely random.

item.title: Negative-Safe Entity: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Either way, at what point do I know if I can post a draft?

If you do not yet have a successful mainsite page, you need two greenlights on a concept before you can post a draft for critique in the Draft Critique forum. Reviewers will be very clear when they are giving a greenlight (and if you're uncertain, you can always ask to confirm).

If you would like to receive feedback on a draft without greenlights, you can ask for draft critique in the IRC chatrooms (though some reviewers may still request that you get the concept reviewed first).

item.title: Counting Sheep: Re: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there TPE_gaming. Let’s take a look at your concept.

I do see potential here. You’ve crafted an emotional narrative that explains the origins of the scp quite while. I’m also clear about the themes you wish to convey. Before I offer the greenlight, however, I do feel there are a couple of bumps you need to smooth out:

The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

One of my major question marks: why are musical boxes morphing into sheep, and vice-versa. I know you’re trying to go for multiple objects as symbols here, but the more you stretch the reader’s imagination, the harder it is to keep them invested in your world. Why not, for example, just take the musical boxes out of the equation? Have the kid still linked to the sheep in some way (maybe he grew up on a farm, for example) and after his death, his spirit lived on in the animals who were his only companions. Or something like that. I just felt the musical boxes were completely random and unnecessary. But I would also like to hear your thoughts and justification if need be.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try to take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: The Wild Hunt: Re: The Wild Hunt
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Atomholic. Let's take a look at your concept.

While I applaud your enthusiasm for mythology and desire to bring them to life, there are much better ways to do it besides simply retelling the entire myth word for word. That's what your Central Narrative reads like at the moment: a list of multiple anomalies that happen one after another without additional context or explanation as to their significance.

This does not make for an interesting narrative. Consider SCP-1826, which also involves elements of the mythic Wild Hunt. Notice how they do not simply list the Hunt as a singular event, but weave it into a modern setting, where the Foundation and other characters are also intrinsically involved. You might need to do that here as well. Don't just re-tell a myth as an scp. Instead, find a unique angle / perspective from which to convey elements of the myth.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I'll take another look. Best of luck for now!
